Discussed the paper "Network Hygiene, Incentives, and Regulation: Deployment of Source Address Validation in the Internet," which measures SAV (spoofing prevention) deployment using the Spoofer Project. #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: for the year ending Aug 1, 2019, 25.2% of tested IPv4 ASes and 32.1% of tested IPv6 ASes had at least one prefix with no outbound SAV filtering. At prefix level, 14.9% of IPv4 /24s (non-NAT) and 12.3% of IPv6 /40s were unfiltered. #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: inbound filtering of spoofed packets (source inside client's own subnet) is less deployed than outbound; 67.0% of IPv4 ASes and 74.2% of IPv6 ASes had at least one prefix not filtering inbound spoofed packets (year ending Aug 2019). #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: comparing May 2006 to the year ending Aug 2019, 18.3% vs 14.9% of IPv4 /24 prefixes and 20.4% vs 30.5% of ASes did not block spoofed-source packets, implying SAV deployment has not generally improved. #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: NATs are not a substitute for SAV. In the year ending Aug 2019, 86.8% of the 2,783 IPv4 ASes tested had NAT-involved tests; 6.4% of NAT IPv4 /24 prefixes still forwarded spoofed packets. NAT failure modes: forwarding spoofed source intact, or rewriting to the NAT's public address. #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: no meaningful correlation between IPv4 prefix age (first appearance in BGP, Jan 2000–Aug 2019 Routeviews/RIPE RIS snapshots) and spoofability; fit f(x)=0.0000262x+0.08 (Figure 5). #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: crowd-sourced Spoofer data is longitudinally sparse—even with the daemonized client, 44% of IPv4 /24 prefixes and 32% of ASes reported in only one week (May 2016–Aug 2019); only 8% of /24s and 23% of ASes had 20+ active weeks (Figure 6). #SAV #Spoofer

Paper finding: per-prefix spoofability prediction model (radix trie of BGP prefixes + /24, chronological train/test) achieved >90% accuracy; recall rose from ~20% in May 2016 to >80% for IPv6 and 50–70% for IPv4 by Aug 2019. IPv4 private-address precision is poor because core filtering occludes edge policy. #SAV #Spoofer

Languages whose words are built by combining morphemes (prefixes, suffixes, base words = affixation) are called inflected or morphologically rich languages; examples: English, German, Spanish, Russian, Latin. #linguistics #morphology

English and Chinese word construction differ in orthography (Roman alphabet vs Hanzi), word formation (affixation on base words vs character compounds), meaning/part-of-speech flexibility, grammar (inflected vs uninflected, position + particles), and tone. #linguistics #english-vs-chinese

Chinese, Japanese and Vietnamese are described as isolating or morphologically poor languages: words don't change form, and new words come from stringing together independent words/characters. #linguistics #morphology

Writing system types besides alphabetic and logographic: syllabic (Cherokee syllabary), ideographic (Egyptian hieroglyphs), abjad (Arabic, consonants only), abugida (Devanagari, consonant-vowel syllables), and picture writing. Most systems mix types. #writing-systems

Discussion on 2023/05/22: writing systems normally represent a spoken or gestured language and usually arise after the spoken language exists (cuneiform, hieroglyphs); sign languages are a case of a visual-manual language developing its own writing techniques. #writing-systems

The National Guard of the United States is a dual-status force: it answers to both the state governor and the federal government, which distinguishes it from other military branches. #NationalGuard

Primary National Guard objectives: disaster/emergency response within the US, providing trained personnel for overseas combat operations, supporting state and federal missions (border security, counter-drug, law enforcement), and maintaining readiness training. #NationalGuard
National Guard members are citizen-soldiers who typically serve part-time with civilian careers, while active-duty personnel serve full-time. #NationalGuard
National Guard training commitment is commonly described as "one weekend a month, two weeks a year"; members also take on deployments/mobilizations ranging from days to months. #NationalGuard

Hurricane Katrina (2005) is a key example of National Guard disaster response: search and rescue, security, supply distribution, and helicopter aviation support in New Orleans and the Gulf Coast. #NationalGuard #disaster-response

The National Guard collaborates with FEMA and the American Red Cross during emergencies, typically operating under the direction of the affected state's governor, helping set up shelters, distribute supplies, run evacuations and SAR, and secure critical infrastructure. #NationalGuard #FEMA

Recent National Guard activations cited: COVID-19 response (testing, hospital support, vaccine distribution), 2020 California wildfires, civil unrest/protest security support, and Hurricane Ida response. #NationalGuard

National Guard history: first colonial militia formed in Massachusetts in 1636; militias fought in the Revolutionary War; the Militia Act of 1903 (Dick Act) unified state militias into the National Guard as a dual state-federal force — roughly 400 years of history. #NationalGuard

National Guard size (per National Guard Bureau, as of 2023): about 445,000 Army National Guard soldiers plus 331,000 Air National Guard airmen, roughly 776,000 total, with units in all 50 states, 3 territories, and DC. #NationalGuard

I discussed Malintzin (La Malinche) with the user on 2023/05/28. Key background: born into a noble family in Mexico's Gulf Coast region, captured by the Aztecs as a young woman, then given to Hernán Cortés as a gift and served as his interpreter, fluent in both Nahuatl and Mayan. #Malintzin #history

Malintzin served as advisor and mediator between the Spanish and indigenous peoples, helping Cortés navigate Aztec society and build alliances; she could communicate with more indigenous groups than Jerónimo de Aguilar, the other Spanish interpreter. #Malintzin

Malintzin married the Spanish man Don Juan Jaramillo. I told the user this was likely a strategic move to gain power, access Spanish resources and privileges, and show loyalty to the Spanish, while also fitting the broader colonial pattern of Spanish men marrying indigenous women. #Malintzin #Jaramillo

The user asked whether Malintzin may have been forced to marry Jaramillo. I answered that it is possible since the relationship is poorly documented and Spanish accounts often portrayed indigenous women as subservient, but that a voluntary strategic marriage is also plausible; the exact circumstances are uncertain. #Malintzin #Jaramillo

I noted to the user that intermarriage between Spanish men and indigenous women in colonial Mexico produced mixed-race children and had a lasting impact on Mexican culture and identity. #Malintzin #colonialMexico
